title: Funding request for EBO-PEP response to Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC
description: EDCTP funded the EBO-PEP project in 2024 to evaluate a post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) strategy against Ebola virus disease, establishing a robust outbreak research platform rapidly activatable across filovirus species. To respond to the current Bundibugyo (BVD) outbreak in Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the consortium seeks to mobilise the infrastructure, partnerships, and operational capacities already in place. Obeldesivir (ODV), an orally administered broad-spectrum antiviral prioritized by the WHO R&D Blueprint, is evaluated as PEP in a randomized trial. Remdesivir (RDV) is proposed for vulnerable populations excluded from the randomized trial. EBO- PEP brings together African and European institutions with complementary expertise in filovirus research and clinical trial implementation in outbreak settings. The overall objective of this project is to increase the portfolio of therapeutic tools against BVD by evaluating a PEP strategy for high-risk contacts in Eastern DRC. The two specific objectives are: (i) to set up a randomised, placebo-controlled phase III trial in Eastern DRC to test the efficacy of ODV used as PEP for high-risk contacts; ii) to set up a parallel prospective interventional cohort to generate evidence on the safety, feasibility, and effectiveness of RDV as PEP in children under 12 years and pregnant or breastfeeding women.

title: Supporting Health Expertise and Climate–Health Engagement at the 2026 Overshoot Conference (Beijing)
description: The Overshoot Conference 2026, co-hosted by IIASA and Tsinghua University in Beijing (24–25 November 2026), will bring together an interdisciplinary, international community to examine the scientific and societal dimensions of climate overshoot, building on the inaugural 2025 conference at IIASA. This proposal requests support to strengthen the health dimension of the conference and Wellcome's engagement with it. First, funding of 40,000 EUR will support the attendance of a minimum of six key experts working on health or health- relevant overshoot topics prioritising those who might otherwise be unable to attend and helping ensure a diverse range of voices in the room. Invitations will be prioritised by IIASA and Wellcome. Second, the budget covers conference registration for approximately three members of Wellcome's Climate & Health team, who will follow the discussions, engage on the health side, and contribute to an internal Wellcome piece on future engagement in this space. Third, it includes modest planning and admin costs for a preparatory joint webinar on climate overshoot which will contain the key contents of he UNEP overshoot report (expected mid of September 2026) and an outlook to the contents of the conference aimed at health experts and Wellcome grantees, timed to follow the UNEP Report.
recipient: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis

title: Sustaining the BME Early Career Researcher Network: Connecting, Developing and Empowering Diverse Research Talent
description: The BME Early Career Researcher (ECR) Network exists to create a more equitable and inclusive research culture by supporting the progression, leadership and visibility of researchers from Black and minoritised ethnic backgrounds across the UK. Building on a decade of impact through its nationally recognised annual conference, the Network will provide year-round opportunities for mentoring, networking, leadership development and collaboration. Over the next five years, the Network will strengthen support for researchers at key career transition points, addressing persistent inequalities in academic progression and the underrepresentation of Black academics in senior leadership. It will expand access to mentoring, sponsorship and professional development, foster interdisciplinary collaborations, and create opportunities for researchers to showcase their work and develop sustainable partnerships. Funding will enable the launch of a BME ECR bursary and travel fund to reduce financial barriers to participation, alongside a dedicated website and digital platform to connect members and share resources. The Network will also generate evidence of effective practice to inform institutional and sector-wide approaches to improving research culture. Through annual conferences and year-round activities, the Network will empower researchers, strengthen career progression, increase representation in research leadership, and contribute to a more diverse, innovative and inclusive UK research ecosystem.

title: Northern Powerhouse R&D; and Innovation Impact Series
description: Following the success of the regional pilot programme (the Liverpool City Region R&D Impact Series), Aid Alliance is proposing the next phase of this work, to be led again by Lou Harbour: a phased regional engagement programme that builds on the momentum, relationships, and lessons developed through the Liverpool pilot. The programme will consist of connected phases: 1\. Phase one: continuing and deepening engagement across the Liverpool City Region, alongside a flagship Labour Party Conference 2026 event in Liverpool designed to elevate these conversations nationally and showcase the region’s leadership around innovation, growth and global health. 2\. Phase two: expanding the model into Greater Manchester through two major convening events and wider borough-level engagement activity, testing how the approach can be adapted across another major regional ecosystem while engaging one of the UK’s most politically influential city regions. 3\. Phase three: exploring the potential for a future “Northern Powerhouse” convening opportunity around Labour Party Conference 2027, focused on R&D and innovation, bringing together partners from across Liverpool City Region and Greater Manchester as part of a wider regional conversation around innovation, growth and public trust.

title: Supporting Advocacy, Thought Leadership and Evidence use Across Three Priority Areas in Africa: Climate and Health, Mental Health, and Global Health.
description: This grant will strengthen African-led advocacy, evidence use and thought leadership across three interconnected priority areas: climate and health, mental health, and global health advocacy. Anchored in Amref’s presence across 35 African countries and its partnerships with Ministries of Health, Africa CDC, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN), and regional and global partners, the programme will support stronger African coordination, collective positioning, visibility, and leadership across key policy, financing, and governance discussions. The programme responds to a critical period for African and global health policy, including COP31-32-33, AHAIC 2027-2029, growing momentum around mental health and adaptation financing, and broader global health architecture reform discussions. It will leverage the convening power of African institutions and platforms to strengthen African voices in policy and financing discussions. Across all pillars, the programme will support the generation, translation, and strategic deployment of African-led evidence and implementation learning to inform regional and global policy work. Through strategic convenings, knowledge products, catalytic ecosystem support, and strengthened institutional capacity, the programme aims to strengthen African influence within climate and health, mental health, and broader global health discourse. Keywords: climate and health, mental health, advocacy, thought leadership, global health architecture, health governance, evidence translation, COP32, health systems resilience

title: GENSCORE Project: Leveraging Generative AI to adapt and enhance the scoring of widely used mental health assessment tools in low-resource context
description: In Nigeria where about 250 psychiatrists serve over 220 million people, contextually accurate mental health screening tools are not just beneficial, they are essential. Our GENSCORE Project aims to develop and validate a culturally grounded, multimodal AI platform/software to improve depression and anxiety screening for Pidgin English, Hausa, and Yoruba speakers in Nigeria. The project will build on our successful pilot to co-develop GENSCORE-DATA v2.0, one of Africa’s largest multilingual mental health dataset, and fine- tune GENSCORE-LLM v2.0 for culturally aligned interpretation. Our culturally relevant model, GENSCORE-LLM, will enable the development of contextually relevant mental health screening (GenPHQ and GenGAD) tools co-designed with people with lived experience and mental health experts. These tools will be integrated into an open-access, multimodal GENSCORE platform combining voice (audio) and self-reported text, facilitating real-time screening and decision support. The GENSCORE tools will undergo rigorous community and clinical validation and benchmarked against SCID-5-CV assessments among 990 participants in language-specific sites: Lagos State (Pidgin English), Abuja, FCT (Hausa) and Oyo State (Yoruba). Robust ethical, governance, and safety frameworks will ensure fairness, data sovereignty, and responsible AI use, with broad national and international dissemination.
programme: Generative AI for Anxiety, Depression and Psychosis

title: Rapid research for community protection in the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)
description: This Wellcome Trust discretionary award proposal sets out a programme to scale rapid, ethical social and behavioural research for the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) PHEIC, declared on 17 May 2026. Anchored in the Africa CDC–WHO continental aim to "stop the outbreak and protect communities," it ensures community evidence drives response while building infrastructure and capability for future epidemic threats, including cholera, mpox and climate- sensitive events. The work has two objectives: 1. deliver rapid research that informs BVD response actions, and 2. establish how outbreak research can be scaled across diverse contexts with quality and ethics sustained. Delivery runs through three work packages. WP1 implements protocol-driven rapid research - building on the WHO inter-agency protocol implemented for mpox, Ebola and cholera - starting in Ituri and scaling to North/South Kivu, Uganda and South Sudan. WP2 creates a "living learning system" with embedded ethics and methods advisory functions and regional convening with Africa CDC. WP3, delivered with Kobo and the Harvard Humanitarian Initiative, provides the secure, nationally owned digital backbone. Key words: community protection, rapid research, rapid qualitative methods, community engagement, risk communication and community engagement

title: E3G Elevating Science Diplomacy & Strengthening EU Resilience
description: This proposal has two elements. i) Targeted science diplomacy initiative to strengthen the integration of climate and health science into international diplomacy ahead of the 2028 Global Stocktake (GST). Led by E3G and University of Pennsylvania Perry World House, it will deliver policy-focused products and invitation-only briefing series for senior climate envoys including from the EU and UN stakeholders, translating evidence on mitigation, resilience, and the climate–health nexus into actionable diplomatic insights. It will equip policymakers with accessible, high quality scientific knowledge, test how science informs negotiation strategies, partnerships, and diplomacy priorities, and identify pathways to embed health-centered climate action into climate-focused global governance. ii) Seed funding to shape the EU Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework while catalysing broader philanthropic engagement in European climate adaptation and resilience policy during a critical 18-month window. The project will seek to build political support for EU action on climate resilience across Brussels and key Member States, develop politically salient narratives, and mobilise actors across civil society, health, workers, business and science. The work aims to strengthen underrepresented voices in European resilience debates and to ensure that the EU framework is socially grounded, economically credible and politically durable.

title: PARTNERS trial
description: PARTNERS is an acronym for 'Platform Adaptive Randomised Trial for NEw and Repurposed Filovirus treatmentS'. PARTNERS is a multi-country, multi-outbreak randomised adaptive platform trial of potential treatments for filovirus disease. This includes Ebola disease (Zaire, Sudan and Bundibugyo species), Marburg disease, and unspecified and emergent filovirus diseases. The primary aim is to identify the effect of included therapies on all-cause mortality at 28 days after randomisation in patients admitted to a healthcare facility with filovirus disease. The treatment comparisons included in the trial are determined by expert consultations convened by WHO.

title: IPI and the IPCC: Defending Science from Politics
description: Established in 1988, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) is the foremost body for compiling and assessing the best available science related to climate change. Since its inception, however, the IPCC process has grappled with the nuanced and multidirectional interplay of science with politics and diplomacy. The IPCC process and its decisions are becoming a toxic negotiation space, where polarization and politicization of this highly scientific body is becoming the norm. Given the central importance of the IPCC’s work to international climate action on health and beyond, and the unprecedented pressure it is under, IPI is focused on strengthening the IPCC process, mandate, and outcomes, including on health. IPI will work closely with key players, provide workshops, and host retreats to protect the integrity of IPCC science, and in doing so strengthen the climate-health nexus. This highly precarious situation needs an injection of new thinking, and as an external party with extensive experience in creating environments that facilitate problem-solving for even the most contentious and sensitive issues, IPI is uniquely situated to conduct this work.

title: London Climate Action Week - Climate and Health
description: London Climate Action Week (LCAW), founded in 2019 by E3G in partnership with the Mayor of London, is a mission-driven, non-profit platform aiming to harness the unique power of London for both global and local climate action. London Climate Action Week (LCAW) has cemented its role as a major global convening moment for climate transition action, with cross-cutting impact and international visibility field building across the climate and health nexus, innovation and science, diplomacy and geopolitics, information integrity, finance, energy, nature, resilience, governance, and more. LCAW has grown into a globally recognised event and platform, convening high-profile individuals and organisations from the UK, EU and wider global markets, and inspiring the creation of climate action weeks in cities worldwide. It firmly stands as an independent, recognisable brand, which is collectively owned by London institutions, stakeholders and the wider climate community, and has a clear focus on public good.

title: WHO Global Health Policy and Systems Research Agenda on Disability Health Equity 2026 - 2030
description: The funding proposal focuses on the development of the WHO Global Health Policy and Systems Research Agenda on Disability Health Equity. Overall Goal: The WHO Global Research Agenda will guide research that generates the evidence policymakers need to reduce health inequities experienced by persons with disabilities. Objectives of the Global Research Agenda: 1\. Define the key knowledge gaps and research areas for evidence generation on health equity for persons with disabilities at a global level over the next five years (from 2026 – 2030). 2\. Strengthen knowledge production for evidence-informed policies, plans and practices relating to disability inclusion in health systems strengthening and primary health care. 3\. Build research capacity on health equity for persons with disabilities by creating a framework for research priorities to be applied and further contextualized at the regional and national levels. The Agenda will cut across different areas, such as communicable and noncommunicable diseases, mental health, social determinants of health such as climate, poverty or gender-based violence, and health- systems strengthening, with a strong focus on low- and middle-income countries. It will target Member States; policymakers, national health research bodies and institutes; global research funders; academic institutions; CSOs and NGOs; intergovernmental organizations; and United Nations agencies.

title: Optimal and biomarker-stratified treatment duration for non-severe pulmonary tuberculosis
description: The standard six-month regimen for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) over-treats people with non-severe disease - imposing avoidable toxicity, cost and treatment burden in low- and middle-income countries. This 24-month award will develop a definitive randomised controlled trial (RCT) in non-severe pulmonary TB to (a) determine the optimal treatment duration; and (b) use a 'test-of-cure' biomarker-stratified treatment duration strategy. Four integrated work-packages will deliver this, through: (1) an individual participant data meta-analysis of transcriptomic biomarkers to predict treatment outcomes, with a prospective biomarker-trajectory sub-study in Zimbabwe; (2) qualitative interviews and a discrete choice experiment with patients and healthcare workers in Zimbabwe and Pakistan, to quantify the trade-off between duration and relapse risk. This will define a patient- centred non-inferiority margin and inform a weighted risk-benefit composite outcome; (3) multi-country recruitment feasibility assessment across passive, active and targeted universal TB testing modalities; (4) iterative international stakeholder engagement - including researchers, policymakers, regulation, industry and communities. The award will deliver a fully specified, methodologically robust and policy-relevant trial protocol, with the potential to: (i) change global TB treatment guidelines; (ii) strengthen trial-readiness through transdisciplinary team building in high-burden settings; and (iii) transform future approaches to defining patient-centred outcomes in treatment shortening trials.
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: University of Nairobi Expression of Interest to lead a Climate & Health Science and Policy Consortium in Eastern Africa
description: The University of Nairobi (UoN) led consortium is well placed to effectively lead the proposed Climate & Health Science and Policy Consortium for Eastern Africa. Its strategic plan explicitly mentions climate change, SDGs, Agenda 2063, and reflects policy alignment with climate adaptation and health outcomes as well as Wellcome Trust's goals for the proposed initiative. UoN has extensive experience and impeccable leadership capability to lead a high impact climate and health consortium based on its track record in research, global science-policy processes such as the IPCC, hosting centres of excellence, both globally recognized internal institutions such as ICCA and UNITID and internationally networked ones like the ARUA-NCD. These are all underpinned by demonstrated leadership in EDI across its research, governance, staffing, community engagement, and research culture. In 2025, UoN notably received a national Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion (GEDI) Award for higher education institutions from the Gender and Disability Development Centre (GDDC). We have developed an inclusive proposal development approach that entails the following: consensus meetings, stakeholder mapping/analysis, co-development processes with stakeholders, inclusion of the wider public through extended surveys, and a well-sequenced and tightly framed proposal writing and review process.

title: Eastern Africa Climate and Health Science and Policy Consortium
description: African Population and Health Research Center and its partners: Addis Ababa University, IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre, CIFOR-ICRAF, and the Population, Health and Environment Ethiopia propose to establish the Eastern Africa Climate and Health Science Policy Consortium. The Consortium brings together partners already engaged in climate-health science, innovations, policy, and action in Kenya and Ethiopia, and across the Eastern Africa region. Our Consortium brings complementary strengths in climate-health science, science-driven innovations, data resources, policy influence, and rich country- and regional-level experiences and presence, ensuring an equitable and robust transdisciplinary approach to climate-health challenges. The Consortium will co-create research and policy ambitions with diverse stakeholders to drive impactful collaboration through: locally-informed climate-health research; innovation scaling up; evidence-informed decision- making for policy and action; strengthening institutions' and affected communities' capacity to respond to climate change impacts; and partnerships that advance equity, diversity, and inclusion across all operations. With a regional mandate, APHRC is uniquely positioned to lead the Consortium, ensuring that research and solutions remain context-relevant and needs- informed, and offering a climate-health vision aligned with Wellcome’s goals. APHRC has extensive experience in managing cross-country and multi-partner programs and proven expertise in evidence translation, capacity strengthening, financial stewardship, and trust-based, inclusive partnership building.
recipient: African Population and Health Research Centre

title: A Philippines-led multicentre clinical trial platform for leptospirosis
description: Leptospirosis is a leading cause of acute bacterial bloodstream infection in Southeast Asia. The Philippines is among the most severely affected, with recurrent flood-associated outbreaks and persistently high case fatality in severe disease. Despite this burden, evidence synthesis of leptospirosis interventional trials reach a consistent conclusion: the field has accumulated trials without generating usable evidence. Fundamental methodological failures - inadequate sample sizes, absent outcome harmonisation, and heterogeneous case definitions - are pervasive. In the Philippines, several single-centre trials are ongoing but operate in isolation, are individually underpowered, and are unlikely to resolve the clinical questions they address.We propose to establish a Philippines-led multicentre clinical trial platform for leptospirosis, the first coordinated international trial infrastructure for this disease. This award will develop a harmonised master protocol incorporating optimised inclusion criteria, a core outcome set, and scalable trial procedures. We will establish a clinical trial network across national and regional hospitals with common infrastructure for recruitment, diagnostics, data capture, and governance. Alongside this, we will build a fully transdisciplinary, internationally networked trial group through structured engagement with collaborating institutions, policymakers, and community stakeholders. Together, these activities will deliver full trial readiness and the partnerships needed to generate definitive, policy- actionable evidence on leptospirosis treatment
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Nigerian Pediatric TB Clinical Trial Consortium (NiPTCC)
description: Nigeria has a high paediatric tuberculosis (TB) burden, yet limited Nigeria- specific evidence exists on how to adopt, operationalise, and scale WHO- recommended shorter treatment regimens for children with non-severe, drug- susceptible TB. Although national guidance is increasingly aligned with WHO recommendations, implementation remains uneven, and Nigeria lacks a coordinated, trial-ready platform to generate local evidence for policy and scale-up. This development award will establish the Nigerian Paediatric TB Clinical Trial Consortium (NiPTCC), a national platform led by NTBLCP, KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Netherlands, KNCV Nigeria, and IVAN Research Institute. The consortium will strengthen governance, identify and prepare trial-ready paediatric TB sites, develop harmonised standard operating procedures, establish data and laboratory quality systems, and build caregiver and community engagement structures. It will also generate implementation evidence on barriers and facilitators to adoption, acceptability, feasibility, and scalability of WHO-recommended paediatric TB treatment regimens across Nigerian health-system contexts. The key outputs will include a functional national paediatric TB clinical trial consortium, a site-readiness and capacity-strengthening package, and a fundable protocol for a future multicentre pragmatic trial comparing WHO-recommended paediatric TB regimens in Nigeria. Keywords: paediatric tuberculosis, Nigeria, clinical trial consortium, implementation science, treatment shortening, WHO regimen, child health, TB policy.
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Mobilising the power of music artists to increase the cultural salience of climate change and engage key audiences in the UK
description: This proposal will enable Murmur to: Build its organisational capacity so that it is able to effectively mobilise music artists and build cultural momentum around the climate conversation, with a strong emphasis on making the links between climate change, climate solutions and health. Work with at least five significant British music artists: at least three that are popular with the Rooted Patriot audience, and draw on Wellcome-funded research to give these artists proof points about the links between climate & health Work with these artists to share messaging about climate change and health via the media and social media Build impactful partnerships between artists and climate campaigns and/or movements with a focus on the links between climate and health (e.g. C40 Cities) Create cultural moments that will help increase the cultural salience of the conversation about climate change and its connection to health - including at least one place-based activation targeted at the rooted patriot audience. Create opportunities for artists to directly influence decision makers through place-based real life activations and through online targeting. Help align and strengthen the ecosystem of partners working on climate and music in the UK Educate artists' teams to support artists messaging credibly on climate and health.

title: Health Evidence and Health-based Arguments in Legal Climate Action
description: The climate crisis is a health crisis. Indeed, the International Court of Justice recently recognized that global warming affects the right to a healthy environment and the right to health as part of a wider planetary health crisis. World-wide, scientists, policy makers, civil society and the public are increasingly aware of the physical and mental health impacts of climate change, and the strain it places on public health systems. Yet, policy action remains lacking, leading to legal action. This project improves understanding and accessibility of health-related arguments and evidence for legal action on climate change. Specifically, it enhances Columbia University’s Climate Litigation Database with improved filtering for health-related cases, and develops accompanying resources and analytical tools to survey, track and analyse how specific types of health arguments and evidence are driving legal action, with special attention to LMIC countries and disproportionately affected communities. Several themed reports, case-studies and analytical tools will enable legal and health scholars and practitioners to work together on specific health impacts and optimally leverage health-related evidence and arguments in policy contexts, devise improved legal strategies, and understand further opportunities for legal action. The project engages relevant stakeholders throughout to ensure optimal development and use of resources.

title: Strengthening Equitable Health Research and Innovation Systems in Africa through AHRIFF and SWEAT
description: Africa is home to rapidly growing scientific capacity and innovation potential, yet this is not consistently translating into sustained health impact at scale. At the same time, shifts in global funding landscapes are placing increasing pressure on traditional grant-based models, highlighting the need for new approaches to financing and sustaining health research and innovation. This proposal is for funding support from Wellcome to co-support a coordinated set of convening side-events and activities designed to bridge these gaps. There will be 3 essential deliverables: \- Co-financing the AHRIFF (Africa Health Research & Innovation Funders Forum) in 2026 and 2027 \- Co- financing the SWEAT AFRICA in 2027 and 2028 \- Convening specialized sessions around innovative financing in Africa, highlighting successful case studies from health and allied sectors and generating a white paper. This proposal offers Wellcome an opportunity to support a strategic, ecosystem-level intervention and advocacy programs that strengthen the foundations of health research and innovation in Africa. By linking convening power with evidence generation and a focus on sustainable financing, the initiative will help ensure that scientific progress translates more effectively into real-world health impact.

title: Developing and evaluating a trial-ready diagnostic-to-enrolment pathway for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections in Nepal
description: Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections are a major global health threat and are associated with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. However, these settings remain underrepresented in antimicrobial resistance clinical trials. One of the key barriers is the inability to generate reliable microbiological results within the strict timelines required for trial enrolment. This study aims to develop and evaluate a time-critical diagnostic-to-clinical decision-to-enrolment pathway for MDR-GNB infections in Nepal to support readiness for international AMR clinical trials such as TREAT-GNB. Using a quasi-experimental before-and-after design, the study will systematically assess delays across microbiological workflows and implement targeted interventions, including workflow optimisation, laboratory capacity strengthening, rapid carbapenemase detection using NG-Test CARBA-5, standardised laboratory–clinical communication pathways, and establishment of a multidisciplinary working group comprising ICU department heads, clinicians, nurses, microbiologists, laboratory personnel, OUCRU Nepal clinical and monitoring leads, and investigators from antimicrobial resistance trials, including TREAT-GNB and ADVANCE-ID, to guide implementation and performance monitoring. The project will also develop a genomic data governance framework in collaboration with the Nepal Health Research Council and assess the feasibility and acceptability of MDR-GNB trial procedures through stakeholder and community engagement. Keywords: antimicrobial resistance, MDR-GNB, carbapenem resistance, clinical trials, diagnostics, LMICs, Nepal, genomic data governance.
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Integrating health into multilateral decision-making processes related to climate change and other relevant thematic areas, with a focus on the G77 and China
description: Through activities under this proposal, SLYCAN Trust will work towards further integrating health into the UNFCCC and other global governance processes by supporting and enhancing strategic alignment, cohesion, and position-building within the G77 and China, the largest intergovernmental group of developing countries representing 80% of the world’s population and including all key developing country groups. This includes provision of support for developing strategic measures for priority agenda items and the overall strategy for the G77 and China; provision of technical and coordination support to the G77 and China for the purpose of enhanced convergence as well as inclusive and collective position-building; coordination activities and creation of spaces for strategic engagement, such as facilitation of gatherings of negotiators around key milestones in the multilateral process (e.g., SBs and COPs); and supporting the evidence-based engagement of developing countries (especially members of the G77 and China, as well as sub-groups) on the climate and health nexus, and interlinkages to multilateral processes related to climate and health. This would include among others key areas of focus such as adaptation, loss and damage, just transition, and security which would relate to climate and health prioritisation.

title: Aligning for Impact: A Global Initiative to Maximize Investments in Research
description: This proposal seeks support to launch and lead the next phase of Aligning for Impact, a global  initiative catalyzed by Wellcome, Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) and Impact Funders  Forum (the Forum). Four integrated projects, supported by a strategic convening and engagement  agenda, aim to reduce the gap between the body of knowledge on research impact assessment and  its use by funders and other research system partners both to invest strategically and effectively in  research that improves lives, and to demonstrate the impact and value of research to decision  makers and the public.      Funding is requested to help establish leadership and management for the initiative, to secure the  endorsement and buy-in of research system champions, to enable overall project management, to  convene key meetings to move projects forward, and to provide research and synthesis support  where needed for projects. This grant will be leveraged to obtain additional support from  participating agencies and granting opportunities. The Forum will continue to contribute significant  in-kind leadership, expertise, time, and convening infrastructure and support, amplifying the value of  Wellcome’s investment.

title: Early initiation of PerIpheral VasOpressors for sepsis Treatment in sub- Saharan Africa (PIVOT-Africa)
description: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality globally, with an estimated 85% of the global sepsis deaths disproportionately occurring in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where access to intensive care and advanced haemodynamic support is limited. To reduce mortality, early management is paramount. Although strategies emphasise intravenous fluid administration, trials in sub-Saharan Africa have demonstrated increased mortality associated with liberal fluid resuscitation. The haemodynamic management for adults with sepsis-induced hypoperfusion within sub-Saharan Africa remains unknown. We hypothesise that early peripherally-administered vasopressor therapy, combined with a conservative fluid strategy, will improve through restoration of perfusion, while reducing fluid-associated harm. To date, this strategy has not been evaluated in sub-Saharan Africa. We will develop a randomised controlled clinical trial (RCT) protocol to evaluate an early peripheral vasopressor intervention compared with usual care in adults with sepsis-induced hypoperfusion in Uganda and Malawi. Protocol development will be informed by structured engagement with policymakers, clinicians, and patients, alongside targeted pilot studies to refine the intervention and trial design. The output will be a definitive RCT protocol designed to inform context-appropriate sepsis guidelines and future policy in sub-Saharan Africa. Keywords: sepsis, vasopressors, fluid resuscitation, sub-Saharan Africa, clinical trial, global health, critical care
recipient: World Alliance for Lung and Intensive Care Medicine in Uganda (WALIMU)
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Qdenga vaccination of dengue-experienced diabetic adults in Pakistan: a development programme to enable a future randomised controlled trial
description: This project collects the clinical, immunological, epidemiological, and operational evidence required to enable a future randomised controlled trial of targeted dengue vaccination in high-risk adults with diabetes in Pakistan. Severe dengue is driven by host vulnerability rather than uniform transmission, with diabetes conferring increased risk of hospitalisation and increased mortality. Although WHO (2024) recommends Qdenga (TAK-003) for individuals with comorbidities, no immunogenicity, safety, or delivery data exist for diabetic populations. Work Package 1 defines vaccine response in dengue-experienced diabetic adults through tetravalent neutralising antibody profiling (PRNT50), glycaemic stability monitoring, and mechanistic immunophenotyping of Tfh–B cell responses. Work Package 2 establishes trial- design parameters, including seroprevalence, severe dengue incidence, recruitment feasibility, and circulating serotype distribution. Work Package 3 delivers a consensus-derived, regulatory-ready protocol through Delphi methodology and stakeholder co-design in alignment with Pakistan’s policy on Immunization. This development programme will generate eligibility criteria, endpoint definition, sample size inputs, and operational pathways for a definitive trial. This work aims to shift dengue vaccination from population- wide deployment towards intervention on the most vulnerable people at risk of severe complications. Keywords: dengue virus, diabetes mellitus, Qdenga (TAK-003), targeted vaccination, immunogenicity, seroprevalence, trial development, severe dengue, Pakistan.
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Investigating Praziquantel Reduced Sensitivity and Resistance in Schistosoma haematobium: A Multi-Country Clinical Trial Development Study Targeting Schistosomiasis in West Africa (Ghana, Burkina Faso, Togo)
description: Schistosomiasis, chronic inflammatory neglected tropical disease causing urogenital and intestinal morbidity, organ damage, anaemia, impaired growth and cognitive development, reduced productivity, and increased susceptibility to co-infections. Importantly, pathology may persist after parasite clearance, indicating that cure does not always restore full health. In West Africa, ongoing transmission, repeated exposure, and rapid reinfection sustain a high disease burden despite repeated mass drug administration (MDA) programmes. Praziquantel remains the only widely used treatment globally, but its extensive use has raised concerns about reduced drug sensitivity and potential emergence of resistance, particularly in high-transmission settings. Persistent prevalence, incomplete cure, and rapid reinfection highlight limitations in current control strategies and the risk of undetected reduced efficacy undermining elimination efforts. This proposal addresses the Wellcome Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award by establishing a foundation for a future multi-country randomised controlled trial (RCT) across Ghana, Burkina Faso, and Togo. We will build a transdisciplinary African-led consortium integrating expertise in clinical trials, parasitology, immunology, genomics, epidemiology, biostatistics, implementation science, and community engagement. A 24-month longitudinal cohort study will define cure rates, reinfection dynamics, early resistance signals, immunological correlates, feasibility outcomes, and effect sizes for future trial design, informing a definitive RCT and strengthening regional research capacity.
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Establishment of Climate and Health Science and Policy Consortium in Eastern Africa
description: Climate change is already intensifying health risks across Eastern Africa. The 2020–2022 Horn of Africa drought left more than 30 million people in Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia facing drought-related food insecurity, and climate change is projected to cause 123 million additional malaria cases and 532,000 additional malaria deaths across Africa between 2024 and 2050. These risks intersect with climate-sensitive livelihoods, food and water insecurity, population mobility, fragile infrastructure and uneven adaptive capacity, increasing vulnerability across the region. However, Eastern Africa’s climate- health response remains constrained by a critical systems gap: fragmented research, weak cross-sector coordination, uneven technical capacity, limited community and policy engagement, and inadequate mechanisms for translating evidence into decisions and practice. This proposal development grant will address this gap by supporting the co-design of an African-led Climate and Health Science and Policy Consortium in Eastern Africa, led by Ifakara Health Institute. The grant will support country and stakeholder mapping, partner consultations, priority-setting, governance design, capacity strengthening, sustainability planning and collaborative proposal writing. The outcome will be a credible regional consortium capable of generating policy-relevant evidence, strengthening regional capacity, supporting evidence-informed decision-making and enabling practical climate-health action. Keywords: climate change; health; Eastern Africa; science-policy consortium; capacity strengthening.

title: Accelerating political readiness for access to TB vaccines
description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the world's leading infectious disease killer, yet the anticipated arrival of novel TB vaccines risks being undermined by political unpreparedness. This project, led by the Global TB Caucus, will map meaningful opportunities for parliamentarians to accelerate readiness for TB vaccine introduction and mobilise parliamentary leadership in a subset of priority countries. Working across up to 15 countries, the project comprises two packages of work. The first maps national and global policy landscapes, conducts stakeholder consultations with parliamentarians, ministries, regulators, civil society and affected communities, and establishes national expert panels to help validate findings. The second translates these findings into targeted political mobilisation, strengthening national TB Caucuses’ capacity to advocate on TB vaccine preparedness, strengthening national panels of experts, supporting regulatory and financing readiness, and equipping parliamentarians to champion TB vaccine uptake publicly. The project will contribute to the WHO End TB Strategy and complement the TB Vaccine Accelerator Council. It will generate a published framework of political levers for accelerating health innovation uptake, offering lessons applicable beyond TB. Keywords: tuberculosis, TB vaccines, parliamentary advocacy, political readiness, health policy, vaccine introduction, new tool introduction, preparedness, demand-generation, low- and middle-income countries, financing, regulatory pathways, global health innovation.

title: A global convening program for implementing integrated sustainable and actionable AMR surveillance
description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) causes millions of deaths annually, yet surveillance systems remain fragmented, underfunded, and inequitable. There is limited genomic integration, weak national ownership, and poor translation of data into actionable public health decisions. This proposal seeks funding to address these gaps by convening global stakeholders to co-develop and implement a roadmap for integrated, actionable AMR surveillance systems that are locally informed, nationally owned, regionally coordinated, and globally aligned. The programme will: • Strengthen nationally owned AMR surveillance systems • Integrate genomics into routine public health practice • Develop a tiered framework to guide country progress • Establish effective governance and sustainable financing models • Ensure surveillance data informs clinical care, policy, and outbreak response The first convening, held in March 2026 at Africa CDC with 109 participants from 52 countries, resulted in the Addis Ababa Call to Action and the formation of six Technical Working Groups addressing governance, data systems, laboratories, financing, translation into action, and national integration. A second convening in September 2026 will bring together key stakeholders to validate findings, agree on implementation pathways, and finalise a global roadmap. Overall, the goal is to move from discussion to practical, coordinated action toward sustainable, nationally owned AMR surveillance systems.

title: 18th Asian Conference on Diarrhoeal Disease and Nutrition (ASCODD)
description: Bangladesh is the site selected for the 18th Asian Conference on Diarrhoeal Diseases and Nutrition (ASCODD) by the organizers. Also tentatively, the 8-10th of December 2026 has been proposed and the site for the meeting is planned for Dhaka, Bangladesh. The proposed theme of the conference is “Reducing deaths due to diarrhoea and malnutrition: Pitching for the last mile”. The outcomes of the 18th ASCODD include: 1\. Provide a forum in which young researchers and leading global health experts can address key scientific and practice-based research, best practice, lessons learned and gaps in knowledge. 2\. Encourage the understanding of nutritional status and their impact on health and response to infections and vaccines in children in LMICs. 3\. Provide a forum for dissemination of use of advanced tools for data analysis using modelling, AI, ML for infectious diseases and vaccines. 4\. Present strong evidence to influence leaders, including key policy makers, young researchers to increase their commitment to typhoid/diarrhoeal/malnutrition prevention, care and treatment, and undertake responsible action. 5\. Reach a wider audience through the webcasting of conference proceedings to regional sub-conferences/meetings. 6\. Improve public awareness of the continued impact of and global response to emerging infection, outbreaks and pandemics diseases.
recipient: International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh

title: Consortium for Advancing Climate & Health Science, And Policy for Sustainable Development in Eastern Africa (CASCADE)
recipient: International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology

title: openScopes AIDDiA: Advancing Infectious Disease Discovery Research in Africa with open-source imaging technology
description: openScopes AIDDiA (Advancing Infectious Disease Discovery Research in Africa; “idea”) will develop and deploy technologies towards overcoming barriers to bioimaging in Africa, and to enable discovery research focused on endemic infectious diseases. We propose a technology development and distribution programme driven by a diverse, multinational team comprising specialist, multidisciplinary expertise located across five collaborating sites in South Africa, Kenya, Uganda, Côte d'Ivoire, and the UK. By combining (i) the deployment of mobile instruments (travellerScopes) that will serve as nodes for training and preliminary investigations with (ii) the development and implementation of advanced microbeScope-based imaging modalities for discovery research focused on live, infectious clinical material, our intention is to seed a sustainable network of active researchers spanning anglophone and francophone sub-Saharan Africa, supported by hubs of technological and research excellence. In linking these hubs to centres focused on hardware design that is responsive to African research needs and the realities of diverse environments, limited resources, and variable infrastructure, we aim to establish a template that illustrates the benefit of partnering technology developers with researchers in discovery research teams – especially in low- resource settings where access to instrumentation alone is inadequate to support sustained uptake of bioimaging for investigations of endemic infectious diseases.

title: Combating drug-resistant Salmonella enterica Typhi bacteria responsible for typhoid fever using artesunate and ciprofloxacin combination
description: Typhoid fever caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi remains a major public health problem in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in West Africa with 762 cases per 100,000 person-years among children in rural areas. Ciprofloxacin has long been an affordable and widely used first-line treatment for typhoid fever. However, the emergence and spread of ciprofloxacin-resistant S. Typhi strains increasingly compromised treatment efficacy. New effective, affordable and accessible treatment strategies are urgently needed to combat drug-resistant bacteria. This project aims to combine ciprofloxacin with artesunate, a safe and widely used antimalarial drug given that current experimental studies have shown that artesunate modulate block the bacteria AcrAB-TolC efflux pump activity and increase intracellular antibiotic accumulation restoring thus optimal bacterial inhibition and ciprofloxacin efficacy against resistant Salmonella. We will evaluate this approach on enrolled patients infected with confirmed ciprofloxacin-resistant bacteria. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either expensive Levofloxacin as control arm or ciprofloxacin combined with artesunate as experimental arm to assess treatments efficacy in both arms over two years using a randomized controlled clinical trial. The outcomes will include bacteria and fever clearance comparison between treatment arms. Keywords: Typhoid fever, Salmonella Typhi, ciprofloxacin resistance, artesunate, Levofloxacin, efflux pump inhibitor, combination therapy.
recipient: University of Sciences, Techniques and Technologies of Bamako, USTTB
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: A multi-scale atlas of human protein interactions across cell types to bridge the genotype-phenotype divide
description: Deciphering protein–protein interactions (PPIs) is essential to understanding cellular function and disease. Existing human interactome maps lack structural resolution, are largely static, and derived from a few immortalised lines. This limits our ability to explain how genetic variants perturb molecular assemblies in specific cell types, and to translate genetics into mechanism. We will deliver the first cell-type resolved, structurally informed atlas of human multiprotein complexes across primary and model cells, under basal and perturbed conditions. Our platform integrates co-fractionation mass spectrometry for broad coverage; in-cell crosslinking MS for residue-level restraints; and next-generation computational modelling able to incorporate experimental constraints and to scale to large assemblies and stoichiometries. We will profile up to ten human cell types with rigorous QC and benchmarking, generate high-coverage crosslinking MS maps for at least two models, and predict structures for millions of PPIs and higher-order assemblies. Multi- modal integration will produce confidence-scored, cell-type specific interactomes linked to genetic variation to illuminate disease mechanisms. All generated datasets, models, protocols and software will be released openly, e.g. via EMBL-EBI archives and a user-friendly web portal, accompanied by training materials and community challenges to catalyse uptake. The resource will enable structural biologists, geneticists and AI developers to accelerate discovery.
recipient: The Trustees of Columbia University in the City of New York

title: Optimising itraconazole-based management for chronic pulmonary aspergillosis in post-tuberculosis patients: a trial development study in Senegal
description: This Development Award will develop and optimise a pragmatic chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) intervention pathway for post-tuberculosis (TB) patients in Senegal, integrating early itraconazole-based antifungal management into routine post-TB care. CPA is a major but under-recognised complication of post-TB lung disease in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where persistent respiratory symptoms are frequently misclassified as recurrent TB, contributing to delayed antifungal treatment and avoidable morbidity. The project will combine structured clinical assessment, Aspergillus serology, fungal microbiology, and feasible imaging strategies to identify probable CPA and evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, pharmacological practicality, and implementation performance of pathway-guided antifungal management. Particular emphasis will be placed on real-world implementation challenges including itraconazole formulation variability, procurement feasibility, rifampicin and antiretroviral drug interactions, adherence, treatment continuity, and pragmatic monitoring approaches in resource-constrained settings. Approximately 300 post-TB patients with persistent respiratory symptoms will be enrolled through routine TB follow-up pathways in Senegal. The study will generate clinical, pharmacological, operational, and implementation evidence required to optimise the intervention pathway and inform a future African-led pragmatic randomised controlled trial in post-TB fungal disease care.
recipient: Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar
programme: Infectious Disease Clinical Trial Development Award

title: Future Directions of African Health Data Systems: A Pan‑African Workshop Series
description: This proposal seeks Wellcome support for a pan‑African workshop series, “Future Directions of African Health Data Systems,” to accelerate interoperable and equitable health data integration across the continent. The series aligns with Wellcome’s priorities on data, science, and health systems by translating emerging AU and Africa CDC frameworks, and major research investments, into practical implementation pathways, with particular emphasis on responsible use of large‑scale, linked data for public and planetary health. Led by Programme Manager Michelle Skelton, in collaboration with Wellcome, Africa CDC, ABI and a dedicated steering committee, the series will draw on expertise in technical architecture, governance and ethics, data science, AI and digital health, and implementation research to shape agendas and maintain strong feedback loops with Member States and communities of practice. Workshops will convene regional bodies (Africa CDC, AU organs, Regional Economic Communities, WHO AFRO), communities of practice, grassroots technical communities, civil society, AI and digital health innovators, and key funders driving health‑system digitisation, including Wellcome, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and the NEPAD/AU Innovation Fund. By intentionally bridging these actor groups, the series will ensure that continental norms and strategies are grounded in implementation realities, and that community‑driven innovation actively shapes regional standards and investments.

title: Establishing a Community of Practice for improved consideration of intersectionality in UK medical research
description: This project will establish a Community of Practice (CoP) to advance intersectional equity in UK biomedical, health and care research. Building on policy outputs, educational materials and networks established by the Equity by Evidence and MESSAGE projects, this CoP will convene people with lived experience, funders, regulators, higher education institutions, academic publishers and researchers to drive coordinated improvement of intersectionality integration in research. The CoP is structured around four objectives: furthering implementation of equitable research policies across race, ethnicity, sex and gender; synthesising best practice evidence when accounting for disability, age and socioeconomic status in research, and the interactions between protected characteristics; monitoring policy impact through a sector-wide Equity Impact Assessment (EIA) framework to evaluate participation and outcomes; and generating educational materials and training to build capacity for embedding intersectionality in research design, data collection and reporting. CoP efforts will reduce fragmentation, streamline expectations of researchers and translate equity commitments into practice to strengthen research’s ability to improve health outcomes for all. Over three years, the CoP will deliver three Policy Labs and co-produced resources centred on stakeholder priorities and lived-experience expertise. Outputs include a scalable EIA framework, researcher training and sector-wide learning, to deliver measurable progress in research equity.

title: Rethinking Misinformation, Health and Human Security
description: Misinformation and disinformation have been ranked by the World Economic Forum and United Nations as top global risks, above extreme weather, armed conflict, and cyber warfare. Their impact on health is severe and growing – from suspended clinical trials and the disruption of vaccination and other health programmes, to climate science denialism and the systematic erosion of trust in health institutions. Yet current response frameworks remain largely reactive and narrowly focused on correcting false information, when the most damaging narratives often operate through emotional manipulation, fear polarisation, undermining of trust, and distortion of perceived social norms - not explicit falsehoods. The Lancet Commission on “Rethinking Misinformation, Health and Human Security” will reframe the dominant understanding of misinformation and operationalise the concept of ‘signal distortion’ as an actionable framework and develop and test ways of intervening to enrich the integrity of the information ecosystem – identifying where and how to intervene to improve the overall quality of information ecosystems while working to build underlying trust. This approach is designed to be operationalised and to outlive the Commission. The Commission will generate clear, policy-targeted recommendations for the audiences best positioned to act – health ministries, multilateral institutions, research institutions, media organisations, technology platforms, and civil society.
recipient: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine

title: Support for experts tackling Aedes-borne arboviruses and applying endosymbionts in vector control at the 3rd Global Congress on Genetic Biocontrol Technologies
description: The African Genetic Biocontrol Consortium in Collaboration with the National Biosafety Authority in Zambia will host the 3rd Global Congress on New and Emerging Genetic Biocontrol Technologies in Lusaka, Zambia, March 15-18, 2027. Experts will share knowledge on innovative strategies for genetic and biological vector control, under the theme “Advancements in Engineered Modification Strategies for Vector Control”. This proposal requests support from the Wellcome Trust to facilitate essential discussions and encourage wide-ranging involvement at the forthcoming Congress on Advancements in Engineered Modification Strategies for Vector Control, focusing on Aedes mosquitoes. The Congress will serve as a distinguished forum to promote scientific advancement and collaborative initiatives in two key areas: (1) Genetic modification (GM)-based methods for Aedes vector control, and (2) endosymbiont-based strategies, including the application of Wolbachia to prevent diseases transmission by Aedes mosquitoes. By highlighting both technological advances and implementation challenges, we hope to accelerate responsible adoption of these strategies in affected regions.

title: FILE Funding Proposal – Using health evidence to support the African Advisory Opinion
description: Against the backdrop of FILE and Wellcome Trust’s successful partnership on the International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (ICJ AO) and our shared strategic focus on the intersection between climate and health, Wellcome invited FILE to share a brief outline of some short-term investment opportunities for next steps at the end of 2025. Three workstreams were shared in a Concept Note by FILE, as priorities for immediate investment: • Workstream A. Supporting the African Advisory Opinion • Workstream B. Health impacts of fossil fuels in the Niger Delta, Nigeria • Workstream C: Catalysing the climate and health legal ecosystem Wellcome has now identified support for the African Advisory Opinion as a priority workstream for immediate funding.
recipient: Stichting Foundation for International Law for the Environment

title: Advancing Africa–Europe Cooperation on Research, Climate Diplomacy and Health
description: This proposal outlines a two-year strategic partnership (2026–2027) between the Africa-Europe Foundation (AEF) and Wellcome to advance Africa–Europe cooperation at the intersection of health, climate and research. It responds to a central challenge: key decisions shaping health outcomes are increasingly made within broader political, financial and climate frameworks, requiring stronger alignment between evidence, policy and investment. Building on a successful collaboration since 2024, the partnership shifts from agenda- setting to implementation, focusing on translating evidence into policy and financing outcomes. It is strategically timed to influence major processes, including the EU Multiannual Financial Framework, FP10, and global climate and economic governance (G7/G20, COP). The partnership is structured around three pillars: (i) high-level Africa–Europe dialogue to engage senior policymakers and shape health and financing agendas; (ii) research and innovation cooperation, contributing to a more equitable and globally oriented FP10; and (iii) climate diplomacy, positioning the climate–health nexus as a driver of cooperation and investment. Through targeted convenings, analytical outputs and policy engagement, AEF will provide a platform to connect stakeholders, strengthen trust, and translate scientific evidence into actionable policy and investment pathways, supporting more resilient and inclusive development outcomes.

title: African mental health community mobilisation: Influencing the 7th Ministerial Summit
description: The 7th Global Ministerial Mental Health Summit—the first to be hosted in Africa—offers a pivotal opportunity to advance rights‑based, person‑centred mental health reform across the continent. Yet lived experience advocates, who are essential to shaping effective and locally grounded solutions, remain underrepresented in global policy spaces. Strengthening their leadership is critical to ensuring that government commitments reflect real community needs and drive sustainable system change. This initiative will enable meaningful, well‑supported participation of African lived experience leaders throughout the Summit process. Through the Global Mental Health Action Network (GMHAN), which connects nearly 10,000 members worldwide and has a strong African base, we will convene a diverse Short‑Term Action Group chaired by lived experience advocates; deliver regional capacity‑building workshops in English and French; and provide travel grants, safeguarding, and logistical support for participation in WHO regional consultations and the Summit itself. We will also co‑host a high‑level Side Event on lived-experience advocacy and research and produce communications outputs that amplify African‑led narratives. By mobilising advocates, strengthening networks, and elevating lived experience leadership, this initiative will ensure that African voices shape Summit outcomes and drive long‑term progress toward inclusive, rights‑based mental health systems across the continent.

title: Harnessing Comparative Genomics to Uncover the Principles of Somatic Evolution and Healthy Ageing
description: Somatic mutations accumulate in our cells throughout life. A subset confer selective advantages that drive the expansion of mutant clones, contributing to cancer and a broad range of age-related diseases. While recent studies have revealed the ubiquity of these processes in human tissues, we lack a general framework for somatic evolution. Why do mutation rates, mutational processes and clonal dynamics vary across cell types and tissues, and which features matter most for preserving resilience as we age? This project pioneers a comparative genomics framework to address these foundational questions. The vast diversity of lifespans and physiologies across species provides a remarkable resource to interrogate the rules of genome maintenance. I will combine ultra-accurate sequencing with a uniquely curated cross-species tissue biobank to produce the first comparative atlas of somatic evolution. By studying somatic mutation and clonal dynamics across 30 species, including cancer-resistant elephants, long-lived whales, and ‘immortal’ invertebrates, I aspire to uncover the evolutionary principles that govern genomic maintenance in ageing tissues. This work will generate insights into the cellular processes that drive age-related decline, identify organisms with exceptional genome stability, and lay the groundwork for evolutionarily informed strategies to improve human healthspan, cancer prevention, and reproductive health.

title: Mentorship as a Tool for Equity: Strengthening Respectful Clinical and Research Learning Environments in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone has made significant progress in rebuilding its health workforce, yet the clinical learning environment for junior doctors remains fragile. Evidence from the University of Sierra Leone Teaching Hospitals Complex shows that over two-thirds of junior doctors experience academic bullying, including belittling, exclusion, and public humiliation. These behaviours are often normalised as a “rite of passage,” contributing to burnout, psychological distress, and intentions to leave the sector, undermining both workforce retention and patient safety. At the same time, there is strong local appetite for change, with clinicians seeking tools to foster more inclusive culture. This project will co-design, implement, and evaluate an equity-based mentoring programme to address these challenges. Through structured training, coaching, and communities of practice, it aims to disrupt harmful hierarchies, strengthen inclusive leadership, and build psychologically safe clinical and research environments. Co-developed with Sierra Leonean clinicians and led by an interdisciplinary team, the programme aligns closely with Wellcome’s priorities on mental health and equitable research systems. Over 9 months, the project will train 50–60 clinicians, support progression into research and specialist training, and generate robust evidence on impact. Outputs include a mentorship toolkit, evaluation report, academic publications, and a scalable model for national and regional adoption.
recipient: The Research Institute of St. Joe's Hamilton

title: Digital Public Infrastructure for Climate and Health (DPI4CH) to advance climate health resilience
description: The World Health (WHO)-World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Climate and Health Joint Programme (Joint Programme Office), with partners, will advance digital public infrastructure (DPI) for trustworthy, integrated and interoperable climate and health data and information systems by extending the Digital Public Infrastructure for Climate and Health (DPI4CH) project through a new 12 month grant April 1, 2026 through March 31 2027. This extension builds on the existing partnerships with Digital Square at PATH and WHO’s Department for Data, Digital Health, Analytics and AI (WHO Digital & Data). To empower health systems to anticipate and respond to climate threats, this extension operationalizes the Wellcome-Joint Programme Office’s vision to build a science-policy-implementation ecosystem where interoperability and collaboration is the default. Moving beyond the initial landscape identification, the primary purpose of this phase is to establish the normative foundation and institutional capacity required to turn climate science into actionable health decisions. By evolving the 'Global Goods' concept into active market horizon scan and analysis, as well as 'ground- truthing' technical guidance through in-country readiness assessments and local adaptation, this investment ensures that digital climate-health solutions are not just available, but can be scalable, standardized, and integrated as a sustainable core of national health and climate infrastructure.
